get.description: Is the app running, and can it reach Neo4j?
Everyone, every link, and where each person sits on the lineage rings.
A generated, fictional family, for trying the canvas at size. Nothing is stored.

put.description: Remember where people were dragged to; a null position puts them back on the rings.

delete.description: Rearrange: everyone goes back to their place on the rings.

put.description: The centre of the tree (none: the oldest ancestor) and how the rings are coloured.

get.description: Find people by name or nickname: every word matches the start of a word.

put.description: Replace everything the person form edits.

patch.description:
Change only what's given: a gender, a date of birth, where they live or where they
were born, for the quick fixes in What's missing and on the map. One Undo
step.

delete.description: Move to the Trash, restorable for 30 days.

post.description: Create a parent, spouse, child or sibling of this person, already linked.
Turn an unknown parent into someone new, or someone already in the tree.

delete.description: The photo moves to profile/previous/ in the person's folder; nothing is deleted.

get.description: The square kept from the photo, so a new crop can start from it.
The whole photo, upright, for choosing a new crop.

What merging someone entered twice into this person would do: rehearsed, then rolled
back. Nothing is written.

post.description:
Merge someone entered twice into this person: their details where this one has none,
their links through the rules, then them to the Trash. One Undo step.

get.description:
Who changed this person, and when, the newest first: as their journal keeps it, kept
by the keeper's computer and travelling with the family.
The life story (Markdown) and its Sources, from biography.md in the person's folder.

put.description:
Save the story. Refused (409, "changed_outside") if the file changed since
`base_version`, e.g. in Obsidian; the answer carries the file as it is now.

post.description: A picture for the story, kept in the person's media/ folder.
Link two people. Refused with 409 and the reason when a rule would break.

get.description: Kinds of parent-child link, with how many links use each.

patch.description: Rename, relabel, hide (active=false), reorder, or change ring placement.

delete.description: Only a kind that no link uses; hide it otherwise.

get.description:
How two people are related, both ways round, with the path between them.
Every statement comes in each kinship language, so switching needs no new answer.
Every relation's words in English, Malay and Javanese, as the answers say them.
The kinship language and the Malay birth-order titles.

put.description:
Choose the kinship language; set the family's Malay birth-order titles. Not
a change to the tree, so there's no Undo step for it.

get.description: Deleted people, newest first. Each stays restorable for 30 days.

post.description: Put someone back, with their files and every link to people still in the tree.

get.description: How a typed date is understood, for the live preview under date fields.

post.description:
Make an export in DATA_DIR/exports: the full archive, GEDCOM 5.5.1, a spreadsheet, or
a copy of the app with the family inside, following its choices: view-only, or to
edit and send back, for someone.

get.description: An export or backup from DATA_DIR/exports, as a download.

The backup archives, newest first, with what each holds; and the backup folder
(BACKUP_DIR), with whether it can be reached.

post.description: Bring in a backup archive from elsewhere, e.g. another disk, to restore from.

Replace everything with this backup. Everything as it is now is backed up first.
Refused (422, "bad_archive") if the archive is damaged: then nothing changes.

get.description: What Undo and Redo would do next.

post.description:
Undo the latest change; with `step`, only if that's still the latest ("not_latest").
Refused (409, "cant_undo") if what it changed has since been changed another way: the
history is then cleared, so nothing made meanwhile is overwritten.
Redo the change undone last.

get.description: Which person you are, for "Me"; none until you've chosen.

put.description:
Choose which person you are, or none to forget. Not an Undo step: it isn't a change to
the tree, like the kinship language.

get.description:
Where this computer stands: signed in or not, its part in a family folder, who's in
it, who's asking to join, and what's in the way, if anything.

post.description: Start signing in to Google: open `url` in the browser, then watch the status.
Forget the sign-in here and give it back to Google. The family folder waits.

Start the family's folder in this Google account's Drive, as its keeper. The status
carries the recovery code, this once.
The recovery code is kept safe: it's never shown again.

get.description: Family folders shared with this Google account, to join.

post.description:
Ask to join the family in a shared folder. The status carries the code to read to the
keeper.
Be the family's keeper again on this computer, from the recovery code.
Share the family folder with a relative's Google account (the keeper's).
Let a computer in, with a role, once its code matches (the keeper's).
Turn away a computer asking to join (the keeper's).
Remove a computer from the family: it can't read what comes after (the keeper's).
Keep in step now, rather than within the minute.
The keeper's answers to this computer's changes, read: not shown again (a relative's).

What a relative's computer sent, compared with the family it was made on and with the
tree now, for you to tick, as changes from a copy are (the keeper's). Nothing is written.

Bring in what's ticked of a relative's computer's changes: a backup first, one Undo step,
and Take back later. It reaches everyone, and the computer hears what wasn't taken.
Take none of a relative's computer's changes; it hears so, with your note.

get.description:
The columns an import reads, as a CSV that Excel opens. With example=true, filled in
with the fictional test family.

post.description:
What an import would change, for you to tick, its questions, and what it would leave
out. The import runs inside the database and is rolled back: nothing is written.

get.description: Earlier imports, of spreadsheets and from copies, newest first.

post.description:
Import the file with these answers and the changes ticked: a backup first, then one
Undo step.

What a copy to edit brings back, compared with what the app knows it started from and
with the tree now: each change for you to tick. The file is only read, never run.
Refused (422) when it isn't a copy to edit ("not_a_copy", "not_to_edit"), is locked without
its password ("locked"), has another ("wrong_password") or is damaged ("damaged"); (409)
when it wasn't made here ("unknown_copy") or is older than one brought in ("older_copy").

Bring in the changes ticked: a backup first, then the people, details and links as one
Undo step, then stories and photos. Take back undoes it all later.

get.description: What an import left out or found different, as a CSV.

post.description:
Undo an import: everyone it added goes to the Trash, with their links; its other links
go; the details it changed go back, and the people it removed come back.

get.description:
Everyone but unknown parents, with where they live and were born, each found on the
map: by your pin for the place, its town, its state's middle, or its country.
The made-up family on the map, spread over real towns. Nothing is stored.

put.description: Put a place the gazetteer doesn't know on the map, or move its pin. One Undo step.

delete.description: Take a place's pin off the map. One Undo step.

chosen.description: The changes ticked, as a JSON list of their ids. Left out: those ticked to begin with.

crop.title: Crop
crop.description: JSON crop in percent; centred if absent

BringIn.title: BringIn
BringIn.description: Bring in what's ticked of a computer's changes, with a note for what isn't.

ChildGroup.title: ChildGroup
ChildGroup.description:
Children of the same parents, eldest first when that is known.

`kind` is None for children by birth; otherwise the kind of link (e.g. adoptive) that
this group of children shares with this person.

ChildrenOrder.title: ChildrenOrder
ChildrenOrder.description: Children of the same two parents, eldest first.

CopyPermissions.title: CopyPermissions
CopyPermissions.description: What relatives may do in a copy to edit: all of it unless switched off.

CopyPreview.title: CopyPreview
CopyPreview.description: What a copy to edit brings back, for you to tick. Nothing is written.

CopyReturned.title: CopyReturned
CopyReturned.description: Which copy to edit came back, as the app recorded it when it made it.

Counts.title: Counts
Counts.description: What the tree's toolbar used to show, and more.

Crop.title: Crop
Crop.description: The kept square, in percent of the upright photo (react-easy-crop's `croppedArea`).

DictionaryWord.title: DictionaryWord
DictionaryWord.description: One language's words for a row of the Kinship dictionary.

FamilyMap.title: FamilyMap
FamilyMap.description: Everyone but unknown parents, with where they live and were born, and the pins.

FillIn.title: FillIn
FillIn.description: An unknown parent becomes a real person: someone new, or someone in the tree.

FolderAnswer.title: FolderAnswer
FolderAnswer.description: The keeper's answer to the changes this computer sent.

FolderAsking.title: FolderAsking
FolderAsking.description: A computer asking to join: its code should match the one its owner reads out.

FolderChanges.title: FolderChanges
FolderChanges.description: A relative's computer with changes waiting for the keeper's review.

GenderedLabel.title: GenderedLabel
GenderedLabel.description: One side of a relationship kind: "adoptive parent", or "adoptive father"/"mother".

GraphLink.title: GraphLink
GraphLink.description: For "parent" links, `source` is the parent and `target` the child.

HistoryStep.title: HistoryStep
HistoryStep.description: One change that can be undone or redone, e.g. "Link Siti and Ali".

HistoryView.title: HistoryView
HistoryView.description: What Undo and Redo would do next.

ImportChange.title: ImportChange
ImportChange.description:
One thing the import would do, which you can leave out. New people, new links
and details changed only in the file start ticked; a removal, a clash, a detail whose
file doesn't say what it started from, or a date that can't be read waits for your tick.

ImportDifference.title: ImportDifference
ImportDifference.description:
A row that is someone already in the tree says something the tree doesn't, and it
isn't offered as a change: the tree has been changed since the file was exported, so the
tree's is the newer. For you to look at.

ImportLeftOut.title: ImportLeftOut
ImportLeftOut.description:
A value or a link that didn't come in, and why; the rest of the row still did. For a
copy: whose it was, in `column`, with no row.

ImportOption.title: ImportOption
ImportOption.description:
One answer to a question: "person:<id>" (someone in the tree), "row:<n>" (a row of the
file), "new" (someone new) or "out" (leave the link out).

ImportSecondLook.title: ImportSecondLook
ImportSecondLook.description: Something that came in but is worth a look, e.g. an unlikely age gap.

ImportSummary.title: ImportSummary
ImportSummary.description: An earlier import, for Settings → Import and What's missing.

JournalEntry.title: JournalEntry
JournalEntry.description: One change to someone, as their journal keeps it: who changed this, and when.

KinExplanation.title: KinExplanation
KinExplanation.description:
"What does this mean?": the answer told with the people on the path, in
English like the rest of the app.

KinPerson.title: KinPerson
KinPerson.description: Someone an answer mentions: the two people, or anyone on the path between them.

KinRelation.title: KinRelation
KinRelation.description: One way the two are related.

KinWord.title: KinWord
KinWord.description:
A statement in one kinship language: its word, and the sentence with it, which
stays English: "Siti is Ali's mak su".

KindWords.title: KindWords
KindWords.description:
A kind's words in another kinship language, e.g. Malay: "angkat", "bapa
angkat" / "emak angkat", "anak angkat". `label` is the kind as a qualifier, as in "abang
angkat".

KinshipSettings.title: KinshipSettings
KinshipSettings.description:
The kinship language and the Malay birth-order titles. Stored in
DATA_DIR/settings/app.json under "kinship".

LayoutUnit.title: LayoutUnit
LayoutUnit.description: One set of rings: a family's own, or a cluster hanging off one person.

Located.title: Located
Located.description:
A place as written, and where it goes on the map: `found` says how. None there means it
wasn't found: a country the gazetteer doesn't know.

MapPins.title: MapPins
MapPins.description: Every pin, kept in settings/app.json, so backups carry them.

MeSettings.title: MeSettings
MeSettings.description:
Which person you are, for "Me". None until you choose. Stored in
DATA_DIR/settings/app.json under "me"; not an Undo step.

MergeDetail.title: MergeDetail
MergeDetail.description: A detail of the two, as the merge treats it.

MergeLink.title: MergeLink
MergeLink.description: A link of the one merged in, and what becomes of it.

MergePreview.title: MergePreview
MergePreview.description: What merging `other` into `keep` would do. Nothing is written.

NewRelative.title: NewRelative
NewRelative.description: Create someone already linked, e.g. "Add child".

Notice.title: Notice
Notice.description: Something worth a second look that was still saved, e.g. an unlikely age gap.

Pair.title: Pair
Pair.description: Two people and what joins them: the links between them, or a kinship word.

PartialDate.title: PartialDate
PartialDate.description:
A date that may be incomplete or approximate: "1950", "Mar 1950", "c. 1920", "1910-1915".

Unknown parts stay empty; they are never filled with a stand-in value.

PersonInput.title: PersonInput
PersonInput.description: The person form. Only the full name is required.

PersonPatch.title: PersonPatch
PersonPatch.description:
What's missing's quick fixes, and the map's: only what's
given changes. A date of birth comes as parts, or typed, like the form's.

Pin.title: Pin
Pin.description:
A place the gazetteer doesn't know, put on the map by hand: everyone who lives or was
born there lands on it.

RelationshipCreate.title: RelationshipCreate
RelationshipCreate.description: Read as "`person_a` is `person_b`'s `a_is`": a is b's mother -> a_is "parent".

ReviewChanges.title: ReviewChanges
ReviewChanges.description: The keeper's answers to the look-alike questions, so far.

Seat.title: Seat
Seat.description: Where someone sits on the rings; the browser draws it.

SharedFolder.title: SharedFolder
SharedFolder.description: A family folder someone has shared with this Google account.

SiblingGroup.title: SiblingGroup
SiblingGroup.description: Children of the same parents whose order isn't known yet.

TurnDown.title: TurnDown
TurnDown.description: Take none of a computer's changes, with a note to say why.
